title: Unique Email Addresses
statement:
An email address has the form `local@domain`: a **local name**, a single `@`, and a **domain name**. Mail systems apply two rules to the local name only, and the domain name is never changed:

- Every `.` in the local name is ignored, so `a.b` and `ab` reach the same mailbox.
- The first `+` in the local name and every character after it (up to the `@`) are ignored. The `.` rule is applied to the part that remains. A `+` in the domain name has no special meaning.

Given a list of `n` addresses, find how many **distinct mailboxes** they deliver to, that is, the number of different results after applying both rules to every address.

Every address contains exactly one `@`, and its local name is guaranteed not to start with `+`. After the rules are applied, the local name always keeps at least one letter or digit.
input_format: The first line contains `n`. Each of the next `n` lines contains one email address (no spaces).
output_format: Print a single integer: the number of distinct mailboxes.
constraints: Addresses use lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `+` and exactly one `@`
The local name does not start with `+` and keeps a letter or digit after the rules are applied

examples.explanation: The first three all become `johndoe@mail.org`. The fourth keeps its different domain, `johndoe@mail.net`. The last becomes `john@mail.org`. That is 3 distinct mailboxes.
The first three all deliver to `ab@x.io` (everything after the first `+` is dropped, dots included). The last one has another domain.

hints: Split each address at the `@` so that you only clean the local name.
Cut the local name at the first `+`, then remove every `.` from what is left.
Put the cleaned `local@domain` strings in a set and print its size.
reference:
import sys

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    seen = set()
    for e in data[1:1 + n]:
        local, domain = e.split('@')
        local = local.split('+')[0].replace('.', '')
        seen.add(local + '@' + domain)
    print(len(seen))

main()
